strings.d1.s0.name: Castle Square Sigismund's Column
strings.d1.s0.tips: A UNESCO old town flattened in 1944 and rebuilt brick by brick; look for the king's column.
strings.d1.s1.name: Royal Castle Warsaw
strings.d1.s1.tips: The royal castle, with Rembrandts and Canaletto's views of Warsaw (used in the reconstruction). Free on Wednesdays.
strings.d1.s2.name: Old Town Market Square Syrenka
strings.d1.s2.tips: The mermaid statue, colourful merchants' houses, the Barbican and the city walls.
strings.d1.s3.name: Zapiecek Pierogarnia
strings.d1.s3.tips: A pierogi chain (in the old town): try ruskie (potato and cheese) and fried pierogi, with kompot.
strings.d1.s4.name: Krakowskie Przedmieście
strings.d1.s4.tips: The Royal Route: Presidential Palace, Chopin benches (they play music), the University and Hotel Bristol.
strings.d1.b0.name: Bar Mleczny Pod Barbakanem
strings.d1.b0.tips: A milk bar in the old town: kotlet (breaded cutlet) and naleśniki (filled crêpes).
strings.d1.b1.name: Warsaw Uprising Monument & Krasiński Garden
strings.d1.b1.tips: The Uprising monument and park; swap in for the column.
strings.d2.s0.name: POLIN Museum
strings.d2.s0.tips: 1,000 years of Polish Jewish history; one of Europe's best museums, with a wooden synagogue ceiling. Free on Thursdays, closed Tuesdays.
strings.d2.s1.name: Ghetto Heroes Monument
strings.d2.s1.tips: Rapoport's monument in front of the museum, where Willy Brandt knelt.
strings.d2.s2.name: Charlotte Menora Plac Grzybowski
strings.d2.s2.tips: A bakery-café next to the Nożyk Synagogue: bread and chałka (braided sweet bread).
strings.d2.s3.name: Nożyk Synagogue
strings.d2.s3.tips: The only synagogue to survive the war; see the ghetto-era houses on Próżna street.
strings.d2.s4.name: Hala Koszyki
strings.d2.s4.tips: A food hall in a 1908 market hall; go in the evening.
strings.d2.b0.name: Jewish Historical Institute
strings.d2.b0.tips: Home of the Ringelblum Archive; swap in for the synagogue.
strings.d2.b1.name: Bar Bambino Mleczny
strings.d2.b1.tips: A milk bar on Krucza street.
strings.d3.s0.name: Warsaw Uprising Museum
strings.d3.s0.tips: The 1944 uprising; the 3D film 'City of Ruins' and a sewer tunnel. Closed Tuesdays, free on Thursdays, book online.
strings.d3.s1.name: Wola Murals Elektrownia Powiśle
strings.d3.s1.tips: A mall and food venue in a former power plant on the Vistula bank.
strings.d3.s2.name: Elektrownia Powiśle Food Hall
strings.d3.s3.name: Copernicus Science Centre
strings.d3.s3.tips: Interactive science, good with children, with a planetarium and a riverside setting.
strings.d3.s4.name: Vistula Boulevards
strings.d3.s4.tips: The riverside promenade: in summer, bars with sand beaches (Cud nad Wisłą), the Syrenka statue and sunsets.
strings.d3.b0.name: Neon Museum Soho Factory
strings.d3.b0.tips: Communist-era neon signs in Praga; swap in for the science centre.
strings.d3.b1.name: Bar Prasowy Mleczny
strings.d3.b1.tips: A legendary milk bar on Marszałkowska.
strings.d4.s0.name: Łazienki Park
strings.d4.s0.tips: A royal park with peacocks and the Chopin monument (free concerts on summer Sundays at 12:00 and 16:00).
strings.d4.s1.name: Palace on the Isle
strings.d4.s1.tips: A neoclassical summer palace on an island, built for Poniatowski.
strings.d4.s2.name: Belvedere Restaurant Łazienki
strings.d4.s2.tips: A smart lunch in the orangery; a park café is the alternative.
strings.d4.s3.name: Wilanów Palace
strings.d4.s3.tips: Poland's Versailles (King Sobieski), with baroque gardens. Take bus 116 or 180; in winter there is a garden of lights.
strings.d4.s4.name: Wilanów Poster Museum
strings.d4.s4.tips: The Polish poster school, next to the palace.
strings.d4.b0.name: Łazienki Amphitheatre Café
strings.d4.b0.tips: A café in the park for a light bite.
strings.d4.b1.name: Ujazdów Castle CSW
strings.d4.b1.tips: A contemporary art centre next to Łazienki; swap in for Wilanów.
strings.d5.s0.name: Ząbkowska Street Praga
strings.d5.s0.tips: The east bank that survived the war: brick courtyards, shrines to the Virgin Mary, street art. 10 minutes by tram.
strings.d5.s1.name: Koneser Polish Vodka Museum
strings.d5.s1.tips: A museum in a former vodka factory with 3 tastings; the Koneser courtyard.
strings.d5.s2.name: Bazar Różyckiego
strings.d5.s2.tips: An open-air market from 1901; pyzy (potato dumplings) straight from the jar.
strings.d5.s3.name: Bar Mleczny Rusałka Praga
strings.d5.s3.tips: An unchanged retro milk bar next to Praga Park.
strings.d5.s4.name: Soho Factory & Neon Museum
strings.d5.s4.tips: A factory complex with a neon museum and cafés.
strings.d5.b0.name: W Oparach Absurdu
strings.d5.b0.tips: A bar with absurdist décor on Ząbkowska; vodka.
strings.d5.b1.name: Warsaw Zoo
strings.d5.b1.tips: The zoo of The Zookeeper's Wife, in Praga; swap in for Soho.
strings.d6.s0.name: Palace of Culture and Science
strings.d6.s0.tips: Stalin's 237 m gift; the terrace on the 30th floor gives a city panorama.
strings.d6.s1.name: Fryderyk Chopin Museum
strings.d6.s1.tips: Multimedia exhibits in the Ostrogski Palace, including his last piano. Free on Sundays.
strings.d6.s2.name: Kafka Powiśle
strings.d6.s2.tips: A bohemian café next to the Chopin museum, overlooking the river.
strings.d6.s3.name: Holy Cross Church Chopin's Heart
strings.d6.s3.tips: Chopin's heart is kept in a pillar here, on Krakowskie Przedmieście.
strings.d6.s4.name: Chopin Concert Chopin Point
strings.d6.s4.tips: An evening Chopin recital in the old town (daily); in summer, free Sunday concerts at Łazienki.
strings.d6.b0.name: Restauracja Zoni Koneser
strings.d6.b0.tips: Modern Polish cuisine in Praga; swap in for the concert.
strings.d6.b1.name: National Museum Warsaw
strings.d6.b1.tips: Matejko's Grunwald; swap in for the Chopin museum. Free on Tuesdays.
strings.d7.s0.name: Saska Kępa Francuska Street
strings.d7.s0.tips: Modernist villas and cafés in a calm east-bank neighbourhood.
strings.d7.s1.name: Skwer Breakfast Saska Kępa
strings.d7.s1.tips: A neighbourhood café for a farewell breakfast.
strings.d7.s2.name: National Stadium from Outside
strings.d7.s2.tips: The red-and-white national stadium, across the Vistula.
strings.d7.s3.name: Warszawa Centralna Airport Train
strings.d7.s3.tips: The train to Chopin Airport takes 20 minutes. Farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Cafe Kulturalna Palace of Culture
strings.d7.b0.tips: A café inside the palace; swap in for Saska Kępa.
strings.d7.b1.name: Museum of Polish History Citadel
strings.d7.b1.tips: A huge new history museum, opened in 2023, at the citadel.
strings.note0: Trams, metro and buses: a 20-minute ticket is 3.40 PLN and a day ticket 15 PLN; use the Jakdojade app. The SKM airport train takes 20 minutes. Public transport is extensive, and trams are essential.
strings.note1: Summer is 22-27°C; look out for Sunday Chopin concerts at Łazienki (July-September 2026), Vistula beach bars and the Warsaw Summer Jazz Days.
strings.note2: Pierogi cost 30-40 PLN, a milk bar meal 20, the vodka museum 60, POLIN 45 and the Uprising Museum 30. Poland is good value, cards are accepted everywhere, and the tip is 10%.
strings.note3: Free days at museums: Royal Castle on Wednesday, POLIN on Thursday, Uprising Museum on Thursday, National Museum on Tuesday. POLIN and the Uprising Museum are CLOSED on Tuesday.
strings.note4: Milk bar (bar mleczny): take a tray, order at the counter, pay at the till; try Prasowy, Bambino and Rusałka.
strings.note5: Try Żubrówka with apple juice, żurek (sour rye soup), bigos (hunter's stew) and pączki (doughnuts; on Fat Thursday, in February).
